arguments.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: one complete original earned-picture illustration for a modern FPV arcade game, a landscape still shown after a level is won.
Style/medium: sophisticated late-1980s / 1990s 16-bit pixel-art illustration, visibly deliberate square pixel clusters and stepped edges, layered environmental detail, restrained dithering, no photorealistic texture, no painterly blur, no 3D render. Rich but disciplined shared palette: deep ink navy and petrol shadows, muted olive vegetation/equipment, warm apricot light and dusty rose accents; blue/yellow accents reserved for the Ukrainian FPV.
Composition/framing: one full-bleed wide 2:1 image, ideally 2048 by 1024 pixels. A cinematic, legible environmental composition, readable as a complete reward still at small phone size. Calm mid-value areas and subdued background threat equipment leave room for bright separately rendered game actors when used later. This is scenery, not a screenshot, tactical map, sprite sheet or contact sheet.
FPV shape: one small recognizable Ukrainian FPV quadcopter silhouette, a narrow dark graphite central body, four thin diagonal arms and exactly four propeller rotors, a tiny camera at the nose, subtle blue and yellow battery strap or ribbon. It is part of the environmental story, not an oversized UI icon or consumer camera drone.
Narrative: fictional Ukrainian defenders' FPV perspective during resistance to a Russian military invasion. Military threat presence is limited to non-graphic fictional Russian invading equipment, subdued and secondary to the setting. The scene shows no identifiable real person and no specific real incident.
Constraints: original composition; do not reproduce any existing game art or recognizable film frame. No people, bodies, blood or gore. No Z markings, slogans, lettering, numerals, labels, logos or watermark. No HUD, border, crosshair, targeting reticle, colored gameplay trail, capture line or baked user interface. Opaque finished scenery filling the whole canvas.
Primary request: Orchard Crossing — a hopeful yet tense spring orchard viewed from a low oblique aerial angle. Blossom trees form irregular bands around a narrow irrigation channel; a worn farm track crosses a small stone culvert, giving the composition a clear diagonal journey into sunlit fields. A wind-bent row of poplars and distant village roofs anchor the horizon. Show one small unmarked olive tracked military vehicle and a dark transport truck halted well beyond the orchard at a muddy road junction, partly softened by morning haze. A compact Ukrainian FPV passes above the near blossom canopy, small enough that the orchard remains the main subject. Fresh white-pink blossom and warm light contrast with wheel scars on the distant road. Avoid the old gateway-and-basket composition; create a new aerial landscape without a foreground gate. Lighting: clear apricot dawn through thin cool mist, subdued military silhouettes, readable petrol shadows.

Primary request: Courtyard Exits — a layered Ukrainian brick rail-repair courtyard seen from a modest elevated corner, looking diagonally across worn paving toward several different exit arches. Asymmetric workshop roofs, exterior stairs, ivy in broken masonry, a few sunflowers beside a sheltered doorway and puddles drying after rain create a lived-in place with several possible paths. In the far service lane beyond one arch, a subdued unmarked armored military car sits partly hidden behind a fallen wall and torn camouflage cover; only its distinctive blocky silhouette and churned mud reveal the invasion threat. One small Ukrainian FPV banks over a roof edge toward the open passage. The central courtyard should remain visually open and the architecture should lead the eye between exits. Create a fresh asymmetric daytime composition, not a centered arch with a large vehicle in the foreground. Lighting: warm late-afternoon apricot shafts, quiet teal brick shadows, dusty rose sky, military equipment darker and lower contrast than the main masonry.

Primary request: Night Crossfire — an original nocturnal Ukrainian riverfront industrial district, viewed across staggered rooftops and an old canal lock toward a distant bridge. Brick chimneys, electrical insulators, warehouse roof vents and a narrow reflection of warm windows in the water create layered environmental storytelling. A small unmarked military communications truck with a folded dish and two distant low armored silhouettes occupy the far bridge approach, restrained and partly hidden in blue night haze. One recognizable Ukrainian FPV with a tiny blue-yellow strap crosses the nearer roofline against an uncluttered strip of twilight sky. No active explosion or tracer fire; tension comes from the hostile equipment and the quiet route through the architecture. Strong distinct silhouette layers, mostly midnight petrol/navy, selective warm apricot windows and dusty rose remnant dusk. The scene must remain legible rather than nearly black. Create a new urban canal composition, no observatory, mountains or aurora.
